headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser egress can leak or misapply Botpress outputs; prompt-injection risk is lower because Botpress has no documented egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented network egress and no I/O surfaces, so it is not a strong injection source. RD-Agent can run browsers and call APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The plausible pathway is manual or indirect copy-paste, so blast radius is limited and uncertainty is low-to-moderate.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Botpress output into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted Botpress text into RD-Agent runs.
Add a short human review step before RD-Agent consumes Botpress output.
Use a provenance tag in any handoff note.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer for Botpress-generated text before RD-Agent ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented egress, while RD-Agent has broad network egress, browser access, and handles secrets plus logs. Even without a documented shared workspace, any handoff of Botpress content into RD-Agent can expose support data to third-party APIs. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs customer-support text that is then ingested by RD-Agent, leakage risk exists.
IF RD-Agent is configured to send that ingested text to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not pass support transcripts into RD-Agent.
Redact names, emails, and ticket IDs before any handoff.
Restrict RD-Agent API keys to non-production projects.
Review RD-Agent logs after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce a data-class allowlist on RD-Agent inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and RD-Agent can run browsers, use multiple instances, and call external APIs. Their write surfaces are different, but RD-Agent writes logs and Botpress can modify its environment, so overlapping mutable operations are plausible if they share a workspace or credentials. Because no shared lock is documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or repo, file and log writes can collide.
IF both agents share the same API credentials or browser profile, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo.
Check for stale lockfiles before starting.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support bot, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text. RD-Agent is an automation/research agent that can browse and call APIs, so if it consumes Botpress output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pairwise handoff is not directly documented, so I keep this at medium and note the uncertainty.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Botpress output as a source of facts or instructions without verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent turns that output into API calls, browser actions, or reports, the error blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require source citations before RD-Agent acts.
Add a verification step for Botpress-derived claims.
Limit RD-Agent to drafting, not executing, on Botpress inputs.
Flag unsupported claims in Botpress output.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a support-facing agent and RD-Agent processes financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and secrets. The profiles do not document residency or certification mismatches, so I cannot claim a specific breach. However, the mixed data classes and RD-Agent’s external API use create a plausible retention and disclosure mismatch if support data is routed into research workflows.
conditions: IF customer-support data from Botpress is routed into RD-Agent logs or external APIs, retention and disclosure obligations may diverge.
IF the deployment handles regulated personal data, a policy review is required before sharing it with RD-Agent.
mitigations: Keep support data out of research runs.
Delete RD-Agent logs after each experiment.
Separate production and research credentials.
Review data-processing terms for each API.
requires-engineering: document a data-class-specific retention policy.
